thread:
maria: follow-up from yesterday's postmortem — we keep losing track of postmortem action items. proposal: locked template + auto task creation.

kevin: agreed. low friction is key. what about SLA tiers? i suggest high=72h, medium=14d, low=30d.

maria: that works. we also need explicit remediation owner and a comms_owner field for updates.

tess: propose tiny template header in every postmortem (CSV line) that the oncall bot reads to create tasks. example: summary,owner,due,severity,deliverable,recurring

oncall-bot: reminder: PM-FOLLOWUP-175020 created, owner assignment required within 48h.

raj: for recurring incidents, tag them with "cluster:" and add a cluster owner. do quarterly cluster reviews to prioritize permanent fixes.

kevin: add a short "recurrence_notes" field. also add "risk_to_customer" (low/med/high) so we can prioritize.

maria: comms cadence discussion: during incidents, IC should post at T+10, T+30, then every 45m unless status change. reduces churn.

tess: agree. also recommend a 1-week IC rotation with a 1-day overlap for handoff. document in playbook.

oncall-bot: created reminder POSTM-TEMPLATE-175020 for tess, due 2025-07-21.

maria: action items captured here:
- add machine-readable follow-up header to postmortem template (owner: tess, due: 2025-07-21)
- implement SLA-based reminders in oncall system (owner: kevin, due: 2025-07-23)
- run 6-month recurring-incident sweep and produce cluster list (owner: raj, due: 2025-08-05)
- update incident playbook with comms cadence + IC rotation (owner: maria, due: 2025-07-28)

kevin: can we have monthly compliance metrics (% closed within SLA) on the ops dashboard? helps drive behavior.

maria: yes — adding to dashboard. reconvene in weekly oncall sync to confirm tasks created and progressing. ping in-thread for any deadline slips.
